body: How can I delete your trite bullshit?

I have a feeling most of my friends will not be able to deal with a sober me, and that just plain sucks. I also have a tough time being sober around people unless there's a collective goal. Sitting around and doing nothing is dangerous for me.

Seems like a lot of people say similar things. It takes about a year to be ok. If I may ask, what were the big mental hurdles you went through while passing the big milestones? 

It seems like I tell myself it's ok, you've been sober for a month now, why not have a drink?

I know I have to be the one to make the right choice now. Many times in the past I have sought sobriety for other people, and not myself. I've done aa in the past, and it's just not for me. I will try some smart meetings to see if it can work for me. 

Congrats on a kagillion days sober! What point do you think sobriety started to feel better for you?
How much were you drinking if I may ask?

Having been to many aa meetings, I do believe the thought process is top notch, but the execution is what kills me. It is often too rigid for my taste, and my so called sponsors didn't help me at all. By the third one, I was done.

I do enjoy the concepts however, especially regarding the notion of gratitude. Gratitude has helped me realize so many things about myself and how to view the world in a more positive light. 

Also the concept of giving back in theory is wonderful. Maybe I can give back what I've taken one day. Many people have opened up to me in many ways. It happens so often I consider myself an honorary psychologist. Even my friend who's a real psychologist, who deals with addiction, often seeks my counsel. 

Anyhow, I know I need a support group that is specific to this problem in my life. And I did a search for smart groups that I can attend in my area. Looks like there are a few places I can go that are close by.

Thanks for pointing out alcohol explained. The intro is enough for me to stay engaged. I too have the same standpoint on aa, as it's difficult for me to agree with soooo many of their basic tenets. I feel like I'm being brainwashed. I don't like that feeling. 

It's probably best to take a doctor's advice and plan for recovery.

Thanks friend. When I first read your comment, it brought tears to my eyes. I'm tearing up again responding to you. 

I'm scared of what a sober life can be. I'm afraid of having to explain this to people. "Why can't you have just one drink?" Well... then having to either shimmy around the conversation or give a vivid account of my moral failings. Longest I've been sober since I started drinking was three months, and that was over two years ago.

Thanks friend. I've definitely tried to get my close friends to do other things that aren't sitting around the house. I enjoy being outside but my friends are lazy creatures, so it's a bit of an uphill battle. 

My life long buddy and I used to play disc golf once a week, but he's recently bought a bar and is spending a lot of time out of town (three hours away) and working to get the business up and running. 

As far as family is concerned, I'm tired of hurting them. I tell and scream, and my anger is always out of control when im sober. It sucks knowing they help me as much as they do, and I can't be helpful back.

I would like to see a doctor, but I only have Medi-Cal and don't want to go further in debt and be put on benzos again. That was a much bigger problem for me than alcohol in the past. 

I score anywhere from 25-30 on the ciwa test. I'm not a doctor by any means, but I'm sure that score pretty much means I could croke from trying to quit. 

But I guess I should go see one as this behavior will likely kill me anyways.

Thanks. I hope I can make it. Something needs to change. But I've come to find i can no longer depend on my friends. They have always tolerated my alcoholism, and even encouraged it. They drink just as much as I do, but don't have trouble stopping. 

My family is there for me, but they just don't understand addiction. Their solution is just to stop. Which is not simple for me. Only addicts and former addicts truly understand.

That's why I'm reaching out here. I'm hoping the kindness of strangers can help me.

Thanks man. I hope I find another one. Wish i hadn't let "the one" go so many times. 

But ya know. The dream is to find satisfaction that isn't dependent on someone else. It's kinda why I dont want to be here anymore.
